purpose: Records the frozen-screen evidence, reason, and implementation usage for the existing Core Visual System V1 token families. No new visual direction is introduced here.

token_families.reason: The six references consistently use morning lake blue-gray, mist white, restrained gold, and a dark legibility overlay.
token_families.usage: Background atmosphere, readable dark text/icons, white capture core, rare meaningful gold, and hero metadata protection.

token_families.reason: Brand/emotional copy, editorial fish and page titles, and restrained data text remain visually distinct across the set.
token_families.usage: BRAND for logo/emotional copy, DISPLAY for titles/species, UI for metadata, controls, measurements, and annotations.

token_families.reason: The content screens preserve breathing room and use scrolling rather than compressing dense information into one viewport.
token_families.usage: Section rhythm, card internals, text relationships, and adaptive runtime layout.

token_families.reason: Cards and circular capture/avatar elements use a consistent soft, natural contour family.
token_families.usage: Annotations, pills, content cards, hero cards, camera button, and avatar surfaces.

token_families.reason: Glass is repeatedly used to maintain readability over the natural world while keeping the landscape quieter than content.
token_families.usage: Primary content, secondary story/content, and low-weight overlay/pill treatments.

token_families.reason: The capture entry and Empty Home scene require calm ambient life while content screens must avoid decorative looping.
token_families.usage: Bobber/ripple/cloud/beam motion, capture-button rim sweep and breathing, and restrained content-screen feedback.
